messages:
Maya: PRD live for 'route-policy + graceful-failover' — linking for cross-team review. Please check acceptance criteria, launch gates, and decision log. Comments by EOD Thu. https://redwood.internal/prd/PRD-1987

Release-Bot: PRD-1987 created by Maya (visibility: product, eng, infra, security)

Jonas: quick perf q: what are the P95 targets and the latency budget for fallback decisioning? Need numbers to size mocks.

Maya: in the doc now: Hosted P95 <= 250ms (256-token baseline), Dedicated P95 <= 80ms. Fallback decision must complete <= 150ms. Burst headroom target is 1.8x sustained for 45s.

Samir: infra: 1.8x for 45s is aggressive on older fleets. Suggest we add an admission-control gate and a cheap-variant fallback to avoid OOMs. Also will need autoscaler tuning.

Olivia: security: confirm no new paths to external endpoints during fallbacks. Also need every fallback decision logged with request_id, policy_rule, and target_model.

Maya: adding acceptance item: "Fallback events must be auditable: request_id, timestamp, policy_id, chosen_variant, and reason." Noted for decision log.

Leila: UX ask: when fallback triggers, how does the customer UI reflect it? Recommend: subtle inline banner "Using alternate model for availability — results may vary" with link to docs.

Tom: QA: can you paste the acceptance checklist so QA can map test cases?

Maya: pasted from PRD acceptance section:

```
- Routing correctness: Requests match policy predicates (region, cost_tier, model_family).
- Failover timeliness: On primary model failure or capacity limit, system selects compatible variant within 150ms.
- Auditability: Every routing/fallback decision emits an audit record and a tracing span.
- Performance: Hosted P95 <= 250ms; Dedicated P95 <= 80ms (256 tokens) under normal load.
- Compliance: For regulated accounts, fallback cannot cross geo boundaries.
- Safety: No PII is sent to non-approved endpoints during any routing event.
```

Tom: good. I'll create test matrix: unit tests for matcher logic, integration for fallback path, load tests for burst behavior, and a chaos test that kills model container.

Nina: CS input: two enterprise customers (Acct X, Acct Y) asked for per-customer routing overrides (opt-outs) to force local-region models. Is that in scope?

Maya: core PRD scoped global policy only to reduce rollout risk. I'll add per-customer override as "post-launch" requirement in decision log with acceptance criteria and owner (CS + Product).

Jonas: rough eng sizing: core policy + failover plumbing ~9 dev-weeks; autoscaler + infra ops ~3 dev-weeks; per-customer overrides ~3 dev-weeks post-launch. Flagging potential cross-team bandwidth.

Olivia: compliance: we must gate EU regulated accounts so fallback never routes outside EU. Add legal review step in gates.

Samir: ops request: add runbook with mitigation steps (force fallback to safe-variant, turn off policy routing, scale up canary pool). I'll draft runbook and attach link here when ready.

Maya: noted. I've added runbook requirement and rollback checklist to PRD. Next steps in doc footer: (1) reviewers comment by EOD Thu, (2) resolve open items in decision log, (3) final cross-team sign-off meeting Fri 11:00am if cleared.

Leila: I'll post microcopy proposals for the banner/toast by 9am tomorrow.

Tom: QA will need a dedicated integration stack with Canary capacity to validate. @Samir can you provision?

Samir: yes. I'll open infra ticket after this thread and estimate 2-3 days to provision.

Maya: thanks everyone — ping me if you can't meet Fri. I'll update the PRD with audit/compliance language and the post-launch items and reping the thread when done.

Jonas: :thumbsup:

Nina: :ok_hand:

Release-Bot: Reminder: reviewers requested to complete review within 48 hours (Jonas, Leila, Samir, Olivia, Tom, Nina).
